title: Stance Analysis of Distance Education in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during the COVID-19 Pandemic Using Arabic Twitter Data
summary: Supervised Arabic stance classifiers enabled analysis of 1,846,285 Saudi Twitter posts about distance education during COVID-19. The sampled discourse was predominantly favorable toward distance education. The finding describes platform content during the sampling period and does not represent all residents or establish wider public opinion.
ai_technology: Supervised Arabic text classification identifies stance in a large Twitter corpus; the model operationalizes the study’s social-science outcome.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The study applied supervised stance classification to a corpus of 1,846,285 Arabic tweets and manually assessed sampled classifications.
evidence.unknown: Twitter users and the study period are a selected population; findings do not represent all Saudi residents.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised Arabic text classification identifies stance in a large Twitter corpus; the model operationalizes the study’s social-science outcome.
